text: Many a man will confess his crimes to a common friend, but I never knew a man who would tell his silly weaknesses to his most intimate one, as many a friend will tell us our faults without reserve, who will not so much as hint at our follies; that discovery is too mortifying to our self-love, either to tell another, or to be told of one's self.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XLIII, to his son, London, July 1, Old Style 1748
